captions.linkedin:
Retail investors think chasing yesterday's biggest one-day winner is alpha. The academic data says it's the most predictably bad bet in US equities.

Bali, Cakici & Whitelaw (Journal of Financial Economics, 2011) ranked stocks by MAX, the single largest daily return over the past month. The high-MAX decile underperformed the low-MAX decile by a wide margin, every month, for 43 years.

The behavior is consistent with prospect theory. Investors overweight tail probabilities. They want the lottery ticket. They overpay for it. The mean-reversion comes the next month.

🔹 LOTTERY METRIC, single largest daily 1-month return
🔹 MONTHLY REBALANCE, 21-day lookback, value-weight
🔹 RETAIL DRIVEN, strongest in low institutional ownership names
🔹 PROSPECT THEORY mechanism, tail probabilities overweighted
🔹 IVOL SUBSUMES, MAX explains the negative idiosyncratic vol anomaly
🔹 HIGH TURNOVER, monthly turnover and short leg friction are real

The effect concentrates in small, low-institutional-ownership, microcap names. High turnover and short-leg costs limit net capture. The signal is real. The execution is the hard part.

Bali, Cakici & Whitelaw (2011) Journal of Financial Economics; educational only.
